correctness.rationale: For prime power \(q\ge2\) and integer \(n\ge1\), the full Steinberg regular-group projection has central kernel \(d\,\overline{\mathrm{St}(g)}/|G|\), so both endpoint operator norms equal d times the mean absolute Steinberg character. The known exact Steinberg-value theorem reduces this to semisimple classes. Semisimple centralizer factorization yields the local rational-class weights. A direct combinatorial local Euler identity, the zeta product for monic polynomials with nonzero constant term, and the q-binomial theorem give the stated all-rank recurrence and product. The first increment is \(-1/(q+1)\), later increment ratios lie in (0,\(q^{-2}\)), proving normalized plateaus, strict decreases, and absolute convergence with the stated tail. Independent exact rational semisimple-type enumeration passed for 36 \((q,n)\) pairs; full \(\operatorname{GL}_2\) and \(\operatorname{GL}_3\) explicit matrix/flag character enumerations passed for four groups. Finite tests do not prove the infinite identity, and no result for nonendpoint p norms is claimed.

originality.rationale: The exact Fourier endpoint norms reduce to a weighted mean absolute Steinberg character, and the all-rank parity-plateau and limiting-product identities are not implied by the inspected published general isotypic projection formula, standard character values, ordinary semisimple matrix probabilities, signed building Euler averages, or regular semisimple class counts. Claim-versus-result implication comparisons were made, not mere title searches. The remaining risk of a differently normalized older weighted character identity is stated explicitly.
residual_risks: A hidden older formula for the weighted semisimple centralizer sum or the same q-Pochhammer coefficient under character first-moment or absolute Euler terminology could subsume the result.
No finite literature search or database search can certify universal novelty; relevant unindexed monographs and papers might contain an equivalent normalized identity.

value.rationale: The Steinberg isotypic block is a canonical central spectral projection in regular harmonic analysis of \(\operatorname{GL}_n\) over every finite field. Sharp induced endpoint norms quantify exact amplification rather than merely give decomposition. The closed weighted-class sum has a nonobvious pairwise rank plateau after degree normalization and a sharp positive Euler-product limit, providing a natural all-rank spectral invariant rather than a random parameter sample or known-table recomputation.
